title: Pearson, Hotelling, and the Origins of PCA
explainer: Principal Component Analysis, the dimensionality-reduction technique central to this lesson, traces to a 1901 paper by Karl Pearson on fitting lines and planes to multivariate data, later reformulated into its modern linear-algebra form (eigenvectors of the covariance matrix) by Harold Hotelling in the 1930s. PCA therefore predates computers by decades - it was first worked out by hand on small sets of physical measurements, long before anyone had a dataset large enough to need it.

title: The Tangled History of k-means: Lloyd, MacQueen, and a 25-Year Gap
explainer: The k-means algorithm has a surprisingly split origin: Bell Labs engineer Stuart Lloyd worked out the standard iterative algorithm around 1957 for a signal-processing problem (quantizing pulse-code modulation signals), but his write-up stayed an internal memo and wasn't formally published until 1982, while statistician James MacQueen independently coined the name 'k-means' in a separate 1967 paper. The one-line clustering call in scikit-learn was effectively reinvented in more than one field before anyone noticed the overlap.
